findings.description: This subnet assigns public IPv4 addresses to every instance launched into it. Because it is associated with a route table containing a 0.0.0.0/0 route through an Internet Gateway, workloads placed here are Internet-routable unless separately constrained by security groups and network ACLs.

This subnet assigns public IPv4 addresses to every instance launched into it. Its association with the route table that has a default route through the Internet Gateway makes launched workloads externally routable unless separately constrained by controls not visible in this excerpt.

The EBS volume does not set encrypted = true or provide a KMS key. Its encryption therefore depends on an account-level default not established in this excerpt, risking storage of attached portal-server data in plaintext at rest.

The instance user-data embeds an AWS access key ID and secret access key. User-data is stored in instance metadata/configuration and may be accessible to users or processes on the instance, exposing long-lived credentials.

The security group permits TCP/22 from 0.0.0.0/0. Because it is attached to portal_server in a subnet identified as public and the configuration includes an Internet gateway, this exposes SSH to any Internet host when routing/public addressing are present.

The security group permits all protocols and ports to 0.0.0.0/0. Attached to the portal instance, this removes egress network restriction and permits unrestricted outbound communications, including data exfiltration or command-and-control traffic.

The S3 bucket used as the VPC flow-log destination has no server-side encryption configuration. Flow logs can contain sensitive network metadata and are not explicitly protected with bucket-level encryption at rest.

The snapshot resource does not configure encryption and the excerpt does not establish that the source EBS volume is encrypted. A snapshot of an unencrypted source volume can retain sensitive disk data without encryption at rest.
